subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Roman Space Telescope
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Roman Space Telescope.

hook.text: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will launch in the mid-2020s. It carries a coronagraph to image exoplanets directly.

buildup.text: Its wide field of view will survey millions of stars. Microlensing observations will detect thousands of new planets.

discovery.text: Roman will find planets down to Mars mass using microlensing—far smaller than any current method can detect at distance.

twist.text: Its coronagraph is a technology demonstrator. If successful, it will prove the concept for directly imaging Earth-like planets.

climax.text: Combined with JWST, Roman will give us the most complete census of exoplanets ever assembled.

punchline.text: Thousands of new planets expected. The next great leap in planet hunting.

quiz.question: What detection method will the Roman Space Telescope primarily use to find new exoplanets?
options: Gravitational microlensing to detect planets as small as Mars
The transit method by staring at a single star field for years
Radial velocity measurements of nearby Sun-like stars

details.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, planned for launch in the mid-2020s, will discover thousands of exoplanets via microlensing and direct imaging.
details.whyItMatters: Roman will complete the census of exoplanet types by detecting planet populations inaccessible to Kepler and TESS — especially in wider orbits and free-floating. It bridges current missions and the future Habitable Worlds Observatory.
takeaways: Will discover thousands of exoplanets via microlensing
Detects planets in wide orbits and rogue planets
Tests critical coronagraph technology for future missions

faq.question: How will Roman find exoplanets differently from Kepler?
faq.answer: Kepler used transits, biased toward close-in planets. Roman uses gravitational microlensing, sensitive to planets at wider separations — including those at Earth-like distances from their star. It will also find rogue planets.

faq.question: Why is the Roman coronagraph important even if it can't image Earths?
faq.answer: It serves as a pathfinder — demonstrating that starlight suppression works in the harsh space environment. The lessons learned will directly inform the Habitable Worlds Observatory's coronagraph, which will need to suppress starlight 100-1,000 times better to image Earth-like planets.
